rationale: Uzbekistan is published on a never-assessed uniform seed vector (2/2/2/1.5/2/1.5/2/1.5, composite 20.3) shared byte-identically by twelve countries at ranks 134-145. This full 40-subdimension assessment replaces the seed with evidence and returns 27.5, a difference of +7.2 points.

evidence.quote: The Single Registry is a management information system jointly developed by the Ministry of Finance of Uzbekistan, the World Bank, and UNICEF to enhance the social protection system through reducing barriers in accessing social protection via digitalization. The registry is aimed to support the effective administration of social protection programmes from applications, verification, and registration to payments and monitoring.

By 2023 the new National Agency for Social Protection and community Inson service centers were delivering aid to roughly 2.3 million needy families, about a four-fold increase from 2017. In mid-2024 the Bank approved an additional $100 million INSON project to improve social care for vulnerable groups.

In February 2026, the government approved a new state program to strengthen penalties for violence against women and children, improve enforcement, expand support services, and introduce measurable benchmarks. However, the International Partnership for Human Rights noted important legal reforms but found serious gaps in implementation, including Uzbekistan's continued use of reconciliation in domestic violence cases and restricted access to shelters, services, and legal aid.

On February 28, 2025, the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention ruled that blogger Valijon Kalonov's psychiatric hospitalization was unfounded and arbitrary, yet he remained detained at time of reporting.

The Uzbekistan government never commissioned an independent investigation into the 2005 Andijan massacre, and authorities continued to deny accountability for the deaths and grave injuries that occurred in July 2022 in Karakalpakstan when security forces used unjustified force against protesters.
Article 120 of the criminal code punishes consensual same-sex conduct between men; authorities prosecuted at least 16 people under this provision in 2025.
In May 2025 a Tashkent court found three police officers guilty of torturing suspects, sentencing two to five years and one month, and one to 10 years imprisonment.

Though the government has ended state-imposed forced labor of cotton pickers in the cotton harvest and has committed to broader reforms, the remaining system of strategic crop cultivation and production in Uzbekistan still creates a risk of forced labor for cotton and wheat farmers.
